description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by enrollment level, sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYLEV and covers both undergraduate and graduate students, with total, male, and female counts across nine race/ethnicity categories.

12-month instructional activity totals measured in credit hours and/or contact hours, reported by institution and student level for undergraduate and graduate activity. The table’s grain is UNITID by instructional-activity level (EFIALEV), and it is distinct from the headcount table because it reports activity hours rather than unduplicated students.

Institution-level academic library data on library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services for degree-granting institutions. Expenditure fields apply only to institutions with total expenditures over $100,000; the survey has been part of IPEDS since 2014-15.

Institution-level data on undergraduate admission considerations, applicants, applicants admitted, admitted students who enrolled, and SAT/ACT test scores for entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking students, reported for Fall 2016. The table covers institutions without an open-admissions policy for entering first-time students; SAT and ACT scores apply only where the institution requires test scores for admission. Writing scores are not collected, and admission-consideration responses include “considered but not required” but not “do not know.”

Awards and degrees conferred by six-digit CIP program, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; counts include total, male, female, and race/ethnicity-specific awards.
Students receiving any degree or certificate, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. There is one record per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID, counting students rather than awards.

Students receiving awards or degrees by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age category. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age groups are under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race/ethnicity, gender, and age are not available in combination.

Programs offered and programs offered via distance education, broken down by CIP program and award level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE; six-digit CIP records report award-level offerings, two-digit CIP records summarize the six-digit programs within the group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals. These program-offering counts are derived from completions awarded during July 1, 2014–June 30, 2015.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL and includes total, men’s, and women’s enrollment, including full-time and part-time counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL and includes total, men’s, and women’s enrollment for all nine race/ethnicity categories, including full-time and part-time counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFDELEV and reports total enrollment, enrollment exclusively in distance education, enrollment in some distance education, and enrollment in no distance education; exclusive-distance counts are further broken down by students’ location relative to the institution, including same state, different state, U.S. state unknown, and outside the U.S.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY. Age enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2016 (even) has data only for institutions that reported it.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, with counts of those who graduated from high school in the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE. Residence enrollment reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2016 (even) is not an optional residence-reporting year and this table is not subject to the odd-year optional collection rule.

Fall enrollment counts for selected major fields, broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. It covers only four-year institutions and only Education, Engineering, Biological Sciences/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business Management and Administrative Services, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, major field, attendance status, and EFCIPLEV.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, applicable only to institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions; institutions with less-than-one-year programs do not have retention data.

Institutional finance data for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards, including revenues, expenditures, endowments, and assets and liabilities. Each record represents one institution; the table is the appropriate public-GASB form rather than the FASB or for-profit form.

Institutional finance data for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards, including revenues, expenditures, endowments, and assets and liabilities. Each record represents one institution; the table combines private not-for-profit institutions with public FASB institutions and is distinct from the public-GASB and private for-profit forms.

Institutional finance data for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards, including revenues, expenditures, and assets and liabilities but not endowments. Each record represents one institution; the table is restricted to the private for-profit sector.

Graduation-rate counts and completion outcomes through 200% of normal time for the 2008 cohort at 4-year institutions and the 2012 cohort at less-than-4-year institutions. Records are defined by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort/graduation-status category (GRTYPE), and include completion at 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time; the 4-year records concern bachelor’s-degree-seeking students, while less-than-4-year records cover the general full-time, first-time undergraduate cohort.

Graduation-rate counts and outcomes at 150% of normal time, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort/graduation-status category (GRTYPE), covering bachelor’s-degree-seeking and other degree/certificate-seeking cohorts at 4-year institutions and the general undergraduate cohort at 2-year institutions; the cohorts entered in 2010 and 2013, respectively. For 2-year institutions, 100%-of-normal-time completions are not available by gender and race/ethnicity.

Graduation-rate counts for less-than-2-year institutions, including students enrolled in 2013 and outcomes at 100% and 150% of normal time, including transfers out. Records are at the institution level, identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), with no gender, race/ethnicity, or financial-aid subcohort breakdown.

Graduation-rate counts and 150%-of-normal-time outcomes by financial-aid subcohort: Pell Grant recipients, subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell, and students who received neither. Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and the financial-aid cohort category (PSGRTYPE); 4-year institutions use the 2010 cohort, while 2-year and less-than-2-year institutions use the 2013 cohort, with bachelor’s-seeking and other degree/certificate-seeking groups represented where applicable.

Fall staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty status, tenure status, and contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which combines occupational category and tenure status; non-tenure-track staff are further split into multi-year, indefinite, annual, and less-than-annual contracts, with multi-year and indefinite appearing as separate categories beginning in 2016.

Full-time instructional staff counts broken down by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, which combines faculty/tenure status with academic rank; non-tenure-track staff also have separate multi-year, indefinite, annual, and less-than-annual contract categories. The table applies only to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001 but became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2016 (even) has data under the annual mandatory rule.

Full-time new-hire counts broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender, with instructional new hires additionally classified by faculty/tenure status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which defines the primary occupation and, for instructional staff, faculty/tenure status; the new-hire period is November 1, 2015 through October 31, 2016, and the table applies only to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001 but became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2016 (even) has data under the annual mandatory rule.

Fall staff counts broken down by occupational category, full- or part-time status, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, which combines occupational category with full- or part-time status. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001 but became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2016 (even) has data under the annual mandatory rule.

Full-time instructional staff counts broken down by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT, which combines faculty and tenure status; the table applies only to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Non-tenure-track staff are split into multi-year, indefinite, annual, and less-than-annual contracts, with multi-year and indefinite appearing as separate categories beginning in 2016.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff counts, salary outlays, average salaries, and equated nine-month salary measures broken down by academic rank, gender, and number of months worked. The row-grain variable is ARANK; staff working fewer than nine months have counts but no salary data.
Full-time nonmedical noninstructional staff counts and salary outlays by occupational category.

Custom comparison-group membership records keyed by the submitting institution’s UNITID, comparison-institution UNITID, and group membership identifier, listing the comparison institutions’ names and states for the 2017 Data Feedback Report.

Survey-component response records keyed by UNITID and survey component, indicating response, nonresponse with imputation, applicability, parent/child or multiple-campus reporting, and revised-data status in final or revised releases.

Institution directory records, one per institution identified by UNITID, containing names, addresses, contact and institutional URLs, active status, and Title IV participation. It also includes derived institutional attributes such as control, institution level, highest award offered, and Carnegie classification.

Institution-level records keyed by UNITID covering educational offerings and award levels, institutional control and affiliations, admissions characteristics, special learning opportunities, and athletic associations.

Full-academic-year student charge records keyed by UNITID for institutions whose programs are primarily measured in credit hours under semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or another academic calendar. Fields distinguish full-time and part-time undergraduate and graduate charges, professional-practice program charges, and the published price of attendance for full-time first-time undergraduates.

Vocational-program charge records keyed by UNITID, with the number of programs and program-specific charges for clock-hour or primarily occupational credit-hour programs. The record covers the largest program plus up to five additional program slots; this component is collected only in odd-numbered years, so 2016 (even) has no data.
Institution-level mission records keyed by UNITID, containing either the institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is available.

Award and enrollment outcomes for four 2008-entering undergraduate cohorts at degree-granting institutions: full-time first-time, part-time first-time, full-time non-first-time, and part-time non-first-time students. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort (OMCHRT), and reports the revised and adjusted cohort size plus counts and percentages completing and still enrolled as of August 31, 2014 (six years) and August 31, 2016 (eight years).

Institution-level counts and total and average dollar amounts of grants and loans, broken down by aid source/type and student group: full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates versus all undergraduates. The first-time group includes federal, Pell, other federal, state/local, institutional, and federal/nonfederal loan aid; the all-undergraduate group includes total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans.

Institution-level average net price and the underlying financial aid amounts for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, separated into students receiving grant or scholarship aid and students receiving Title IV federal aid. At public institutions, both groups are limited to students paying in-district or in-state tuition.

Institution-level counts of students and total dollar amounts receiving military, servicemember, or veteran benefits, broken down by Post-9/11 GI Bill Benefits versus the Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program and covering both undergraduate and graduate students. This collection is reported only in even-numbered years, so 2016 (even) has data.
